> "The Complaint of Peace" is a work written by Desiderius Erasmus in 1517. In it, Erasmus argues that the way to achieve true peace is through the teachings of Christ. He criticizes those who use violence and war to spread their ideas, stating that 'the standard of salvation' should not be used to justify the taking of human life. Erasmus argues that true Christianity is characterized by love, meekness, and humility, and that the doctrines and morals of the Reformers are no different from those of the Catholics they criticize. He challenges his readers to consider whether the 'Evangelical' generation is any more virtuous than those they condemn, and urges them to turn away from violence and sin and embrace the peace and love of Christ.
